title: Usage entropy equalizer for cross-route token harmonization
creator: Maya Hernandez
description:
Design and implement a streaming + batch job that normalizes cross-route token attributions using an entropy-based weighting model. The goal is to reduce noisy double-counting when a single user request fans out to multiple internal routes (e.g., embeddings + generation + rerank) and to make late-arriving events deterministically reconcilable without wholesale replays. This job will produce a single canonical 'harmonized_token_claim' per upstream request_id that downstream billing jobs can consume to compute per-tenant cost and attribution.

Scope: streaming Flink job for near-real-time harmonization, a nightly backfill component for historical correction, schema changes to the harmonized ledger, dashboards for monitoring, and a rollout plan that includes shadow runs and canary write-through to the legacy ledger for verification.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming job emits harmonized_token_claim records with stable keys for >99.9% of requests in staging
Backfill run corrects historical duplicates for a 7-day window and matches expected token totals within 0.5% of manual samples
Downstream billing pipeline consumes harmonized records without schema errors and unit tests for reconciliation logic cover edge cases (late arrival, partial failure, replay)
Canary can write harmonized records to isolated ClickHouse table and roll back cleanly on data drift
Latency SLO: 95th percentile harmonization latency < 250ms for streaming path under normal load
technical_notes: Input streams: token_event (Kafka topic), request_manifest (Kafka topic) — use event-time processing with watermarking and 2 minute allowed lateness

Core algorithm: construct per-request attribution vector, compute normalized weights using Shannon entropy penalty to prefer concentrated attributions when signal quality is high, fall back to priority rules when entropy is ambiguous
Dedup strategy: stable request_id + deterministic fingerprint of route contributions; use Bloom filter checkpoints to avoid reprocessing hotspots
Storage: write harmonized records to 'harmonized_ledger' ClickHouse table with partition by event_date and shard by tenant_id; also produce S3-serialized daily snapshots for audit
Backfill: Beam job reading S3 raw-token-batches to produce historical harmonized records; incremental checkpointing to support restart
Idempotency: harmonized records include version and canonical_hash; downstream consumers should apply last-write-wins with version enforcement
Observability: expose per-tenant drift metric (harmonized_tokens / raw_claims) and per-route entropy histogram in Console dashboard

qa_notes: Create synthetic scenarios that fan-out to 3+ routes with varying token shares and validate that the harmonized sum equals original request token count
Inject late-arrival events (up to 2 minutes) and verify stable reconciliation without double incrementing tenant counters
Run backfill on a 48 hour slice in staging and compare against manual sample aggregation; record variance
Test restart and checkpoint behavior of Flink job to ensure no duplicate harmonized writes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Shadow (3 days): run harmonizer in read-only shadow mode for 100% traffic and compare outputs to legacy attribution in dashboard
Phase 2 - Canary writes (1 week): write harmonized records to isolated ClickHouse table; run reconciliation jobs and finance sampling; no downstream billing impact
Phase 3 - Soft switch (2 weeks): enable harmonized reads for non-billing analytics and keep billing on legacy ledger; monitor drift and error budget
Phase 4 - Cutover: flip billing consumers to harmonized_ledger with 1-hour rollback plan; keep legacy ledger in audit-only mode for 30 days
Rollback: removal of harmonized write is safe; consumer should fall back to legacy ledger and replay last 24 hours if needed
notes_for_sre: Flink job needs autoscaling knobs for Kafka partition hot keys; recommend initial parallelism = 64 and monitor task backpressure
Alerting: failures writing to ClickHouse, sustained watermark lag > 90s, harmonized/raw ratio drift > 5% over 15m window
Runbook: on ClickHouse write errors, switch harmonizer to shadow mode and notify data-platform; for sustained watermark lag, increase resources and investigate skewed tenant traffic
postmortem_considerations: If cutover causes billing variance >1% for top-50 tenants, engage finance and run immediate rollback. Capture incident runbook entries, include sample diffs and reconcile policy decisions in a postmortem document. Plan to widen sampling and add tenant-level simulation harness if needed.
